summary: In ancient Greece, the growth of private wealth led to the replacement of mother-right with father-right inheritance, weakening early clan equality.
context: Engels traces the early history of classical Greece. As private property accumulated in individual households, male-line inheritance replaced communal clan inheritance, marking the beginning of class division in Greek society.
